newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil telecoms still Merrill buys.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil telecoms still Merrill buys.

text.p: -- Merrill Lynch & Co said in a report it is maintaining its buy recommendations on Brazilian telecoms firms Telebras and Telesp.

-- The brokerage said the firms may benefit last month's changes in Brazilian tax laws, which now include a provision for a tax credit for approximately 15 percent of capital spending on fixed assets.
-- "We caution, however, that there are many unanswered questions related to the issue," it said, adding it is still unsure if the firms qualify.

-- If Telebras qualifies, the credit could increase 1996 after-tax earnings by 100 million reais to 150 million reais ($0.30/ADR-$0.45/ADR) and 1997 earnings by 500 million reais to 575 million reais ($1.37/ADR-$1.57/ADR), it said.
"This amounts to a potential increase in 1997 earnings of 11.5 percent to 13.5 percent," the statement said.

-- For Telesp, after-tax earnings would rise by 20 million to 50 million reais (0.38 reais to 0.94 reais per 1,000 shares) in 1996 and by 100 million and 150 million reais (1.88 reais to 2.82 reais) in 1997, it said.
-- "That represents a 10 percent to 12 percent potential increase in 1997 earnings," it added.
-- Merrill Lynch said it is not changing its earnings forecast just yet as the firms are still awaiting clarification of the law.
-- "However, we expect the market the market to react positively as investors become aware of the potential tax savings that appear to be incorporated in the new law," it said.

-- Telebras's American Depositary Receipt was up 1/2 to 80 3/4, its preferred was up 17 percent at 82.64 reais and its voting common was flat at 68.30 reais at 1510 local/1410 EDT on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange.
-- Telesp preferred was up 0.99 percent at 205.00 reais at 1510 local/1410 EDT on the Sao Paulo bourse.
